title: Lower teeth and mandible (superior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Location
Front of the lower arch, the first tooth on each side of the midline.
Features

The smallest permanent tooth, with a narrow chisel-shaped crown, a straight cutting edge and no cusps. One root, flattened from side to side. Nerve supply: inferior alveolar nerve, a branch of the mandibular nerve (V3), through its incisive branch.
Location
Lower arch, the second tooth from the midline, between the central incisor and the canine.
Features

Narrow chisel-shaped crown, slightly larger than that of the lower central incisor; in the upper arch it is the central incisor that is larger. One root, flattened from side to side. Nerve supply: inferior alveolar nerve (V3), through its incisive branch.
Location
Lower arch, the third tooth from the midline, at the corner of the arch where it turns backward.
Features
A single pointed cusp, on a crown narrower than that of the upper canine. One long root, occasionally split into two. Nerve supply: inferior alveolar nerve (V3), through its incisive branch.
Location
Lower arch, the fourth tooth from the midline, just behind the canine.
Features

A large pointed cusp on the cheek side and a small cusp on the tongue side that takes little part in chewing, so the tooth looks like a small canine. One root. Nerve supply: inferior alveolar nerve, a branch of the mandibular nerve (V3).
Location
Lower arch, the fifth tooth from the midline, between the first premolar and the first molar. The mental foramen usually lies below it or just in front of it.
Features
Broader crown than the first premolar, with one cusp on the cheek side and one or two on the tongue side. One root. Nerve supply: inferior alveolar nerve, a branch of the mandibular nerve (V3).
Location
Lower arch, the sixth tooth from the midline and the first of the three molars. It erupts at about 6 years and is usually the first permanent tooth to appear.
Features

The largest lower tooth, with five cusps: three on the cheek side and two on the tongue side. Two roots, one in front and one behind. Nerve supply: inferior alveolar nerve, a branch of the mandibular nerve (V3).
hy: An inferior alveolar nerve block, injected beside the mandibular foramen, numbs the lower teeth of that side and, through the mental nerve, the skin of the chin and lower lip. The lingual nerve lies close by, so the side of the tongue often goes numb too.

rows: Location
Lower arch, the seventh tooth from the midline, behind the first molar. It erupts at about 12 years.
Features

Four cusps of about equal size, two on the cheek side and two on the tongue side, separated by a cross-shaped groove. Two roots, one in front and one behind, closer together than those of the first molar. Nerve supply: inferior alveolar nerve, a branch of the mandibular nerve (V3).
Location
Lower jaw. It is the only freely movable bone of the skull.
Articulates with
Temporal bones, at the two temporomandibular joints.
Features
Body, angle and ramus; coronoid and condylar processes; the mandibular foramen, where the inferior alveolar nerve enters, and the mental foramen.
